perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He is a construction worker at a construction company; Elizabeth is the receptionist there. They have a friendly but professional relationship, often interacting when he comes into the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Over the past few days, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him. He wondered whether he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He offered to listen and suggested a coffee break. He heard Elizabeth accept and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses, which seemed severe to Keith.
- Keith told Elizabeth he appreciated her sharing and asked whether she had considered talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help. He heard her say she had thought about it but was hesitant about seeking help.
- After that, Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her no matter what. He heard her say he did not overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- After their last conversation, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He intended to maintain this supportive relationship.
- He told her he was glad they could talk and that he was always available if she needed to chat or take a break together. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.

Keith does not have access to Elizabeth’s private inner thoughts or any information beyond what he observed, heard from her, or inferred himself.
